m1a1_aim_sa_aus.name: M1A1 AIM SA
m1a1_aim_sa_aus.authority: Main ruled the Australia line on 2026-11-02 (DECISIONS) on the owner's request the same day ("flesh out south african and australian tank trees", "no senntinnel please"). The Australian Army's M1A1 AIM SA (59 from 2006-07) on the fleet's plain M1A1 build with the Australian kit the photographs show: the TMAPU in the left rear of a lengthened two-tier bustle rack, the call-sign plate, the kangaroo, the disruptive three-tone and the owner's heavy field net to the muzzle (2026-11-02). No registered 3D comparison exists. Numerical 3D comparison remains unverified.
m1a1_aim_sa_aus.envelopeBasis: The as-built envelope of the fleet's M1A1 (9.77 m over the gun, as published) under the field net, its garnish reaching 3.86 m across the 3.66 m skirts; the tallest point is the TMAPU's exhaust stack (the build carries no whips).

m1a2_sepv3_aus.name: M1A2 SEPv3 (Aus)
m1a2_sepv3_aus.authority: Main ruled the Australia line on 2026-11-02 (DECISIONS) on the owner's request the same day ("flesh out south african and australian tank trees", "no senntinnel please"). The Australian Army's M1A2 SEPv3 (75 under LAND 907 Phase 2, from 2024) on the fleet's SEPv3 source study with its 'mounts' Trophy fit (the brackets, no launchers or radars: "fitted for future installation"), the CROWS-LP, the stock skirts with no ARAT, the kangaroo, the three-tone and the owner's heavy field net to the muzzle (2026-11-02). No registered 3D comparison exists. Numerical 3D comparison remains unverified.
m1a2_sepv3_aus.envelopeBasis: The as-built envelope of the SEPv3 study (9.81 m over the gun) on the stock skirts under the field net, its garnish reaching 3.87 m across the 3.66 m skirts; the tallest point is the whip.
